 Benchmarks ·

 Blog post ·
 runanywhere.ai 
 

 TrnRT is an open inference engine for large language models on AWS Trainium. It serves an OpenAI-compatible API
from one trn2.48xlarge , runs decode as NKI megakernels (about one kernel per layer half), and keeps a prefix cache
across device and host memory. GLM-5.3-Flash is the first supported model; more open models are on the way. 

How we built it, with the AgentX results: Serving GLM-5.3-Flash on one Trainium2 box with NKI layer megakernels.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Where TrnRT stands

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

On InferenceX AgentX, which replays real coding-agent sessions, one TrnRT
engine (8 Trainium2 chips, half a trn2.48xlarge ) delivers more tokens per dollar than one 8-GPU H200 node up to 16
concurrent users, and 3.5-5.2× an H100 node's from 12 to 32 users. All three run GLM-5.3-Flash's FP8 weights and are
priced at AWS's Capacity Block list prices.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Users Tokens per $: trn2 ÷ H200 Tokens per $: trn2 ÷ H100 P90 interactivity, tok/s per user: trn2 / H200 
 --- --- --- --- 
 1 1.64× 1.52× 62.2 / 272 
 4 1.75× 1.74× 41.8 / 235 
 8 1.61× 2.01× 25.8 / 168 
 12 1.34× 3.53× 17.1 / 138 
 16 1.07× 3.82× 14.2 / 87.8 
 24 0.86× 5.16× 11.4 / 78.7 
 32 0.81× 4.95× 10.7 / 50.1 

 Where we're behind. Each trn2 user is slower: P90 interactivity (end to end, the wait for the first token
included) is 10.7-62.2 tok/s per user against H200's 50.1-272. At 24 and 32
users H200 delivers more tokens per dollar (0.81-0.86×), and on the 8K/1K fixed-length recipe, which has no prefix reuse,
trn2 delivers 0.56-0.76× H200's. Where a decode step's time goes is in
docs/RESULTS.md.

 InferenceX AgentX harness 1.0.12, canonical workload, one hour per point; ratios compare the same concurrency. The
1-8 user points use MTP at InferenceX's golden acceptance length (2.519; trn2's measured acceptance is 2.20). Prices,
AWS Capacity Blocks list, read 24 Nov 2026: trn2.48xlarge $2.235 per Trainium2 chip-hour ($35.76 per instance-hour),
p5.48xlarge $5.970 per H100-hour, p5e.48xlarge $6.866 per H200-hour. trn2 ran TrnRT's internal builds on Neuron SDK
2.32 (GSM8K 97.4-97.7% on the MTP builds, strict exact match, 5-shot, all 1,319 problems; a needle test passed on the
host-tier restore); this release's builds are graph-equivalent to them, and a device run of release 0.2.0 itself is
pending. GPU numbers are InferenceX's public runs; we report no accuracy score for them and did not check them. Every
table, source run and the method:
docs/RESULTS.md. 

 Highlights

 Feature What it does 
 --- --- 
 NKI megakernels One fused kernel per layer half for decode: KDA attention, the fused DSA layer, mHC and the MoE FFN. 
 1M-token context Sparse attention (top 2,048) and linear attention, with fixed-size state. 
 Prefix cache A radix tree over FP8 KV pages, plus a host-memory tier for evicted pages and state checkpoints. 
 Two engines per box Each engine is tensor-parallel over 32 logical NeuronCores, behind a session-affine router. 
 Three builds latency , balanced (the default) and throughput , each tuned for a band of users per engine; --preset auto --users N picks one. 
 Agent-ready APIs OpenAI chat, completions and Responses, the Anthropic Messages API, the native /generate and /tokenize : streaming, tool calls, reasoning output and n choices. 
 Structured outputs JSON schema, regex and EBNF through xgrammar, plus penalties and thinking budgets, each behind a flag. 
 Scheduling First-come, longest-prefix, shortest-prompt and priority scheduling, queue limits and five prefix-cache eviction policies. 
 Offline compile Every graph is built on a CPU host; the serving box loads them and compiles nothing by default. 

 Quickstart

You need Docker, a trn2.48xlarge to serve on, and any x86 64 host to compile on. New to Trainium? Start with
docs/AWS.md.

 1. Build the image (Neuron SDK 2.32 (neuronx-cc 2.27), Python 3.13)

 

 2. Build the compile cache (any x86 64 host, no NeuronCore needed; takes hours)

 

 3. Serve (on the trn2.48xlarge , with $OUT/cache and $OUT/nki copied over)

 

 4. Call it with any OpenAI client

 

The full guide covers what each step needs, start-up checks, the three builds and every flag:
deploy · API · configuration.

 Supported hardware and models

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Target Status 
 --- --- 
 AWS Trainium2 , trn2.48xlarge (16 chips, 2 engines × TP 32, LNC 2) ✅ Supported 
 GLM-5.3-Flash (320B MoE, 18B active, FP8, 1M-token context) ✅ Supported 
 More open models 🔜 Coming soon. Request a model 

GLM-5.3-Flash is where TrnRT starts. The engine, router, caches and compile pipeline are built to carry more model
families, and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describes what a new one needs.

 Benchmarks

SemiAnalysis AgentX replays real coding-agent sessions. One
 trn2.48xlarge ran it at a 1M-token context with 32 concurrent agents, for one hour per point:

 Decode batch Requests / min Tokens / min Decode tok/s per user (p50) First token, cached (p50) $ / M tokens (spot) 
 --- --- --- --- --- --- 
 4 19.3 2.36M 46.6 76.73 s $0.061 
 8 25.2 3.02M 29.4 28.82 s $0.047 
 12 (default) 28.9 3.57M 22.3 6.53 s $0.040 

Tokens count input (cached input included) and output. Spot price: $8.60/h, us-east-2, 3 Nov 2026. On a capacity block
at $35.76/h, the batch 12 cost is $0.167 per million tokens. Full tables, cold-prompt latencies, long prompts and
methodology are in docs/RESULTS.md.

These numbers were measured with an earlier build of TrnRT, at release 0.1.0's batch presets, which this release's
builds replace. This repository passes these checks against that build
(docs/KNOWN ISSUES.md):

- Graph equivalence: EQUAL on all 32 ranks, for all 157 graphs that build compiles in the default batch-12
 configuration.
- Outputs: byte-identical to that build's on 384 of 384 requests.
- Serving: the two-engine serve in the Quickstart passed end to end on the device at release 0.1.0. On
 this release it has run end to end on CPU only so far; the device run is pendi

install.title: Quickstart
install.html:
You need Docker, a trn2.48xlarge to serve on, and any x86_64 host to compile on. New to Trainium? Start with docs/AWS.md.

1. Build the image (Neuron SDK 2.32 (neuronx-cc 2.27), Python 3.13)

git clone https://github.com/RunanywhereAI/trnrt.git && cd trnrt
docker build -f docker/Dockerfile \
  --build-arg TRNRT_VERSION=$(python3 -c 'import trnrt; print(trnrt.__version__)') \
  --build-arg TRNRT_REVISION=$(git rev-parse HEAD) -t trnrt .

2. Build the compile cache (any x86_64 host, no NeuronCore needed; takes hours)

OUT=/data/trnrt REV=eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a
mkdir -p $OUT/nki $OUT/work
trnrt() { docker run --rm -e HF_TOKEN -v $OUT:$OUT \
  -v $OUT/nki:/var/tmp/nki-intermediate-cache trnrt "$@"; }
trnrt compile shapes zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --revision $REV --out $OUT
trnrt compile decisions --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --revision $REV --out $OUT
trnrt compile capture --out $OUT -- --model $OUT/shapes
trnrt compile compile --out $OUT --work-root $OUT/work
trnrt compile strip --out $OUT

3. Serve (on the trn2.48xlarge, with $OUT/cache and $OUT/nki copied over)

hf download zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --revision eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a \
  --local-dir /models/GLM-5.3-Flash
docker run --rm --privileged --network host --ipc=host \
  -v /data/trnrt/cache:/cache \
  -v /data/trnrt/nki:/var/tmp/nki-intermediate-cache \
  -v /models/GLM-5.3-Flash:/model \
  -e NEURON_LIBTORCH_CACHE_ROOT=/cache \
  trnrt serve --model /model --port 8000

4. Call it with any OpenAI client

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="unused")
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="glm",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a haiku about Trainium."}],
    extra_body={"session_id": "my-session"},  # keeps a conversation on one engine's prefix cache
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content)

The full guide covers what each step needs, start-up checks, the three builds and every flag: deploy · API · configuration.
